indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: Not visible in uploaded extraction (p.36). Not invented.
indicator.objective: Demonstrate understanding of the causes, symptoms and prevention of food-borne diseases

skills.description: Recognise that food-borne diseases are illnesses caused by eating or drinking contaminated food or water.
Identify causes of food-borne diseases (e.g. germs, dirty food, uncovered food, contaminated water).
Identify common symptoms (e.g. diarrhoea, vomiting, stomach pain, fever).
Give examples of food-borne diseases named in the curriculum (cholera, diarrhoea, typhoid fever).
Identify ways to prevent food-borne diseases (washing hands, covering food, drinking safe water, washing fruits).
State what to do if someone contracts a food-borne disease (drink safe water, see a health worker, tell an adult).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Food that looks clean cannot cause sickness.
Food-borne diseases spread only through the air.
Washing hands is not important before eating.
Diarrhoea is normal and needs no attention.
Only adults can get food-borne diseases.

questions.stem: What is a food-borne disease?
options: An illness caused by eating or drinking contaminated food or water
An illness caused by playing in the sun
An illness caused by sleeping late
An illness caused by running fast
hints: It comes from food or water.
questions.explanation: A food-borne disease is an illness caused by eating or drinking food or water that contains germs.
questions.misconception: Food-borne diseases spread only through the air.

questions.stem: Which of these can cause a food-borne disease?
options: Eating uncovered food with germs on it
questions.explanation: Eating uncovered food that has germs on it can cause a food-borne disease.
questions.misconception: Food that looks clean cannot cause sickness.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common symptom of a food-borne disease?
hints: It affects the stomach and toilet habits.
questions.explanation: Diarrhoea is a common symptom of food-borne diseases.
questions.misconception: Diarrhoea is normal and needs no attention.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of a food-borne disease?
hints: It is spread through dirty food or water.
questions.explanation: Cholera is a food-borne disease. It is spread through contaminated food or water.
questions.misconception: Cholera is spread through the air.

questions.stem: Which of these helps prevent food-borne diseases?
questions.explanation: Washing hands before eating helps prevent food-borne diseases by removing germs.
questions.misconception: Washing hands is not important before eating.

questions.stem: Ama ate food that had been left uncovered near a refuse dump. She later became sick. What type of disease is this most likely to be?
hints: The food was exposed to germs.
questions.explanation: The sickness is most likely a food-borne disease because it came from eating contaminated food.
questions.misconception: Food that looks clean cannot cause sickness.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of food-borne diseases?
options: Covering food with a clean cloth
questions.explanation: Drinking contaminated water can cause food-borne diseases because the water contains germs.
questions.misconception: Food-borne diseases spread only through the air.

questions.stem: Which set lists common symptoms of food-borne diseases?
questions.explanation: Common symptoms of food-borne diseases include diarrhoea, vomiting, stomach pain and fever.
questions.misconception: Diarrhoea is normal and needs no attention.

questions.stem: Which of these is a food-borne disease that causes serious diarrhoea?
hints: It is linked to dirty water.
questions.explanation: Cholera is a food-borne disease that causes serious diarrhoea and vomiting.
questions.misconception: Cholera is spread through the air.

questions.stem: Why should food be covered?
options: To keep germs and flies away
questions.explanation: Covering food keeps germs and flies away, helping to prevent food-borne diseases.
questions.misconception: Covered food cannot get contaminated.

questions.stem: A learner has diarrhoea after eating contaminated food. What should the learner do?
options: Drink safe water and tell an adult
hints: Drinking safe water helps replace lost water.
questions.explanation: The learner should drink safe water to replace lost fluids and tell an adult, who can take them to a health worker.
questions.misconception: Diarrhoea is normal and needs no attention.

questions.stem: What is a food-borne disease?
answer: an illness caused by eating or drinking contaminated food or water
a disease caused by eating dirty food or water
illness from contaminated food or water
hints: It comes from food or water.
questions.explanation: A food-borne disease is an illness caused by eating or drinking contaminated food or water.
questions.misconception: Food-borne diseases spread only through the air.

questions.stem: Which of these practices can cause food-borne diseases?
options: Eating food that has been left uncovered
Covering food with a clean cloth
hints: Flies can land on uncovered food.
questions.explanation: Eating food that has been left uncovered can cause food-borne diseases because germs and flies can get onto the food.
questions.misconception: Food that looks clean cannot cause sickness.

questions.stem: Name two symptoms of a food-borne disease.
questions.explanation: Common symptoms of food-borne diseases include diarrhoea, vomiting, stomach pain and fever.
questions.misconception: Diarrhoea is normal and needs no attention.

questions.stem: A pupil is about to eat an orange bought from the market. What should the pupil do first to prevent a food-borne disease?
options: Wash the orange with clean water
Share it with friends without washing
hints: Fruits can have germs on the outside.
questions.explanation: The pupil should wash the orange with clean water before eating to remove germs on the outside.
questions.misconception: Fruits do not need washing.

questions.stem: Explain why drinking contaminated water can cause disease.
answer: because the water contains germs that can make you sick
contaminated water has germs which cause illness
germs in the water can enter the body and cause sickness
questions.explanation: Contaminated water contains germs. When you drink it, the germs enter your body and can make you sick.
questions.misconception: Water from any source is safe.

questions.stem: Name one cause of food-borne diseases.
hints: Think about dirty food or water.
questions.explanation: Food-borne diseases are caused by eating contaminated food or drinking contaminated water.
questions.misconception: Food-borne diseases are not caused by germs.

questions.stem: Name two food-borne diseases.
questions.explanation: Examples of food-borne diseases include cholera, diarrhoea and typhoid fever.
questions.misconception: Only malaria is a food-borne disease.

questions.stem: A classmate has been vomiting and has diarrhoea after eating food from a street vendor. What should you and your classmate do?
answer: tell the teacher and take the classmate to a health worker
tell an adult and get help from a health worker
inform the teacher and ensure the classmate drinks safe water and sees a health worker
